SID driver work array cleared by the round initialization loop at $1E46. Music data ends immediately below it.
Resident title startup at $8DC0–$8DD1 clears both pages before using the initial work area.
Zero-filled gap between the end of the scroll-bound handler at $43E8 and the next routine at $4413. The resident instruction-reference sweep found no direct or indexed references.

Zero padding after the sprite register clear and before the metatile pointers. The nearby raster pointer arrays are indexed by seven states. Read and execute watches in the title, worlds, bosses and ending registered zero hits.

Zero padding between the NMI return and the following raster IRQ entry at $220D.
Zero padding before the projected collision columns at $2650. The three initialized collision arrays begin at $2650, $2669 and $2682.

comments.text: Title raster handler $9259 increments this byte. The title logic can use successive values as a display clock.
Y coordinates in the latter part of the 25-slot display array. Zero means the slot is inactive for the current sprite projection.
Scratch byte used to preserve an object scan index or an intermediate bound through a nested call.
Fine horizontal motion countdown used by $3F67 and $3FBF while the player has the falling flag.
Even byte offset into the scroll handler directory at $1AC4.
Player's special motion selector. Input dispatch at $0DF0 separates ordinary, riding and swimming movement.
Low three bits carry the fine X scroll state. The camera routines update it modulo eight.
Low three bits carry the vertical fine scroll. The collision probes subtract it to locate the displayed row.
Descending VIC sprite color index starts at six and is decremented through zero to $FF.
The sequence initializer sets it and the idle test at $59C1 clears it when the audio mode permits.
Title Audio Type toggles this byte. Sound-effect eligibility and music restoration test it separately.
Index into the current metatile definition, combining column and row offsets.
Column position added to a screen row address when placing a fresh column of glyphs.
Counts the rows already written by the fresh-column renderer. At twenty rows it exits.
Offset with bit 2 toggled by $1D1D to identify the active playfield screen.
Player X copied into the render-side positions for sprite drawing.
Player Y published to the sprite raster handlers.
VIC sprite pointer for the first player layer, commonly paired with the next pointer for the second layer.
Color or display-effect choice updated by temporary effects such as $962D.
Render-side copy of the player's ninth horizontal position bit.
Fractional advance accumulator whose carry gates one-pixel Y adjustments in the mounted motion paths.
Small workspace between the ride-edge accumulator and the active weapon selector.
Adjacent weapon and mount state initialized in the resident image and changed in the movement code.
The gun-equipped mount saves the prior weapon here before selecting weapon four.
Fine motion accumulator used at $1AD5 before the scroll handler takes a step.
Values one and two are selected by active left and right input respectively and choose the matching pair of player sprite layers.
Six bytes saved at $0B96 for player X/high bit/Y and three camera fields.
Two per-round position coordinates selected from tables by $4095 and used in the rescue-window tests.
Two reduced world-space coordinates used to plot the minimap marker and compare Tiki with the captive's location.
Camera X less the configured base at $0633, used to calculate the player's reduced map coordinate.
The bytes immediately before the minimap masks support the plotting and display state.
One set bit per position within a glyph row. OR with this mask plots the player pixel.
Inverse masks used to erase the previous player dot before writing the new one.
Offsets that lead the marker to its row in the character-sized minimap glyph grid.
Four segment offsets combined with the selected row before updating $8220.
Last glyph-row index written by $0DDE so the next update can remove the previous marker.
Stored horizontal bit index for erasing the last minimap pixel.
Tiki's off-screen-capable X reduced to minimap units by the position-to-marker calculation.
One row coordinate obtained by shifting Tiki's screen Y down five bits, before adding camera position.
Active-low direction and fire bits read from joystick or synthesized by the keyboard handler.
Countdown before choosing another indexed sprite pair for the corresponding motion state.
Two-pose index updated by $1257 and used in the two direction tables.
Two sprite base pointers selected for facing two by the motion animator.
Two sprite base pointers selected for the opposite facing.
Enables the mounted movement path toward the upper camera edge.
Enables the corresponding downward camera adjustment.
Selects one of the jump curve sections and limits repeated up-input acceleration.
Index added to the jump curve phase offset before reading a vertical step.
Accumulated vertical change across the jump's ascent steps.
Two per-shot vertical velocity bytes used by the gravity projectile update paths.
Two countdown bytes reloaded before increasing the corresponding vertical delta.
Direction and mode flags for the player shot slots.
Countdown before the corresponding shot begins testing terrain.
Prescaler for changing the jump curve phase during an ongoing jump.
Offset added to the current curve index by $1A26.
Stored last fire state. The trigger path compares against it to detect a new press.
Prevents immediate repeated jump initialization until the corresponding movement or input condition clears.
Per-phase index offsets into the ascent profile, selected by the active jump phase.
Six bytes of the additive random state. $1AAB computes a new byte and shifts the recorded history.
Little-endian entry points to panel update routines in the $86xx and $87xx ranges.
Counts fine steps still left in the current scroll movement.
Number of bytes copied by the dual-matrix transfer loop at $1DB1.
Remembers which pending movement count has already caused a matrix transfer.
Forty temporary color bytes used by the raster split shift routines to carry a source row across the two unrolled loop groups.
The upper set of six panel character codes. The stepping routine at $9EAF compares the animated byte against this table.
Starting indices loaded as the panel changes toward its target sequence.
Six final character codes checked by the opposite stepping direction.
Current six animated panel character codes copied into status cells by $9E56.
Current character index for the six-cell panel effect.
Timer controlling when one panel character moves toward its target.
Player's remaining life state. The life-icon drawing at $8772 uses it as an index count.
Score held as six displayed digit codes. $8793 increments a selected decimal place and propagates carry left.
Used to detect a change in the leading score digit and increase available credits within the existing limit.
Preformatted world-round suffix and name field copied into the score table after a qualifying run.
Zero-based world selector. The transition at $0A00 advances it and $5B02 converts it to the disk file's digit.
Zero-based round selector within a world. $4095 combines it with four times the world index to read initialization values.
The final boss exit sets this flag at $4714 so $5C9D loads GO, then jumps into the ending at $A000.
Initial byte of the round object stream copied by $41E9. $2968 starts its descending object scan at this index.
Screen codes copied into the first six rows of the $8800 screen by $1E8D. They form the score, credits, timer and border while the playfield scrolls below.
Four color values are read at $9602 for one VIC sprite layer. The next four-byte window starts one byte later and serves the other layer.
The timed effect takes colors for two sprite layers from shifted four-byte windows at $078E and $078F.
Screen codes for the out-of-credits message, copied by the announcement at $0853.
Screen codes for the common title lines displayed in the round introduction.
Screen codes for the selectable music, effects, joystick and keyboard descriptions.
Index zero through two for Start Game, Audio Type and Control Type. Up and down move the corresponding sprites.
The boot image contains a repeated $28/$00 pattern between the menu work and the main code. Indexed accesses to the option strings stop before this group.
Boot entry from F's stack-page receiver. It resets the stack and selects RAM under the BASIC and KERNAL ROMs while keeping I/O visible.
Clears zero-page work bytes, builds the title screen and sets up round state. Credits and the player status decide whether to wait for a start, return to the menu or enter play.
Re-enters the round initializer after a local round change or disk overlay. The main loop services pause, input, object movement, collision and display updates.
Clears the screen, draws the out-of-credits message, supplies the title with six credits and calls the reset-to-world-one loader before restarting the menu.
EOR #$01 on $0687 toggles the pause bit and either copies seven characters from $0692 into the status panel or blanks them.
After round index three, increments the world, loads its files through $5B02 and goes back to the round initializer at $0819.
Increments the round. Within-world disk loads occur at world four round four and world five round three. Other rounds reuse the disk package already in RAM.
Combines the sprite X high bit with its low byte to produce the half-pixel X entries used by the box comparisons at $222D.
Twenty-five half-resolution X coordinates made by $0A31 from positions and ninth bits. The overlap tests at $222D use them.
Compares the round's captive coordinates with the camera window. It fills one display object slot with the captive sprite and sets its visibility flag while the cage is in range.
Uses the playfield probes to change the swimming state, initialize the related movement flags and make step calls into the six-character panel update.
Increments the transition count before calling sound effect nine.
Packed decimal time's minute byte. Round initialization writes $02 and the timer check at $0B66 tests for zero minutes.
Reloaded to $19 before the packed-decimal timer subtracts another second.
Uses a prescaler at $0B20, then decimal subtraction on the seconds. A borrow resets them to $59 and subtracts a minute. Reaching both zero calls the TIME UP path.
Prints the packed decimal seconds and minutes in the status panel. At 00:20 it sets the warning state and requests sound $12.
Seven screen codes for the time-out message copied to the status panel by $0B87.
Copies the TIME UP screen codes to $8897 and increments the time-out flag at $0337.
While $0324 is clear, copies Tiki's position and the scrolling coordinates to the six-byte set $054B-$0550.
Returns from the collision handler without starting a hit when the protection flag blocks it.
Skips collision handling when the protection byte is set. It routes an active hit sequence to its animation, or starts it when any of four object overlap flags is set.
Marks the sequence active and selects the death or exhausted-lives sound and waiting length. While it runs, it updates the player's falling sprite frames before taking the life-handling path.
Drains the pending camera movement after a hit by stepping the probes, screen copy and camera updater until $05CC is clear.
Clears the projectile records in slots two through zero, including their positions and vertical stepping state.
Waits until the tick byte at $0320 is nonzero, then consumes one tick before resuming the caller.
Reduces Tiki and camera coordinates to a marker position, clears the prior bit and plots the new one by changing the glyph bytes at $8220.
Branches by movement mode, checks active-low directional bits, updates the facing and walk pose, and detects the edge of the fire input before asking for a new shot.
The mounted-input path sets this value to $FF. $1AD5 uses it when advancing the fine horizontal scroll accumulator in movement mode one.
Chooses a collision-probe offset for the mount, applies left and right input only when the adjacent tile passes the probe, and updates Y on up input.
Four base pointers for the right-facing animation variant of the mount.
Four base pointers for the other facing's corresponding animation.
Two-bit selector into one of the four-cel mount tables.
Countdown reloaded to eight before advancing the mount's sprite selector.
Uses current facing and mount type to choose the first of two sprite layers. A mount-state flag selects a four-position animation cycling on an eight-count timer.
Copies Tiki's X and its high bit to the selected mount slot. Uses mount type and facing to choose its Y offset and display pointer.
Vertical direction parameters used by the mounted up-input path as it changes its fine Y accumulator.
Fine Y accumulator used to decide when the rider advances one screen pixel.
Moves the rider one pixel right when scrolling is at its bound or the screen threshold permits it. Otherwise sets the rightward scroll request.
Moves the rider one pixel left under the corresponding camera-bound and screen-position tests, or requests the leftward scroll.
On expiry of an eight-count delay, alternates two pose indices and chooses a left or right pair of sprite pointers.
Counts down before the rising effect advances its sprite and moves diagonally again.
Moves the active effect diagonally upward using its saved left or right direction, changes the glyph counter and advances the sprite until it reaches the end of that direction's range.
While the upward flag is active, selects a straight or diagonal camera direction from Tiki's X and facing, then tests and nudges Y.
Adds an immediate step byte to the accumulator at $0544. The caller uses the resulting carry as a one-pixel timing gate.
Adds the other patched immediate step to $0544, again returning carry from that addition.
Tests the downward flag and the lower map bound. When the player is near the central column, chooses a diagonal direction using the facing and side probes.
Scans three rideable object slots. Given an enabled overlap from above or below, records the mount and its orientation, switches the player state and clears airborne flags.
Matches the mount's display pointer against its supported forms. Some pointers set the mount kind, and the weapon-equipped kind preserves the prior weapon and selects weapon four.
Services the three mount records. A hit can detach the current rider or drive a four-step burst animation before retiring the object.
Uses the lower solid-tile probe and current Y before beginning a jump. During an active jump, repeated up input can advance its stored jump phase.
Marks the jump state, clears the phase and height counters, requests the basic effect and sets the initial input timer.
Finds a free projectile slot and invokes its firing effect. The projectile starts near Tiki with a horizontal offset and direction selected by his current facing.
Visits both projectile slots and dispatches to the trajectory handler for the current weapon in $0487.
Per-shot Y step values used by the oscillating shot at $17B2.
Updates the projectile's alternating sprite and color, checks the on-screen bounds, advances X by four pixels in the appropriate direction and applies the projectile's vertical step.
Moves the projectile with its Y delta and three-pixel lateral step. It increments its vertical delta on a timer and changes state after a solid tile test.
Zeros the occupied flag, vertical coordinate, ninth X bit and velocity for slot X. Resets its gravity counter to six.
Moves a fixed-shape shot twelve pixels left or right and retires it at the corresponding screen limit.
Shows one of two launch cels for four passes, then advances a right-going shot six pixels and retires it outside its valid range or on a tile hit.
Shows the left launch cel for four passes, then moves the shot six pixels left. Clears the projectile on a solid probe, hit flag or boundary.
Uses the jump phase and row of $064C to adjust Tiki's vertical position, maintaining the separate ascent and descent counters.
Temporary low-bit offset from Tiki's Y alignment used by $422F.
Clears the jump and drop flags, inhibits an immediate repeat and realigns the player's Y to the active character row.
Immediate return when the player motion handler needs no further state updates.
Adds three bytes of the five-byte history with carry set and shifts that history by one position, exposing the latest output at $05B6.
Eight little-endian handler addresses. $1AFB uses the even movement selector as a byte offset and patches $1B0A's JMP.
Immediate RTS target for the path where the subpixel accumulator advances without carrying.
Applies the fine-position accumulator test where required, then transfers control to the selected scroll handler through the patched jump at $1B0A.
The fine scroll step consumed by the movement handlers. They use modulo-eight arithmetic and shift whole character cells when it wraps.
Consumes a pending movement count, adjusts sprite-relative X, advances the fine X field and shifts color RAM right at a cell boundary.
Subtracts the scroll step from relevant X positions and toggles the stored ninth bit on a borrow. Tiki's position moves only when the probe and movement flags allow it.
Adds the scroll step to four sprite X positions and toggles their ninth bits on carry. Uses the opposite probe to adjust Tiki.
Subtracts the fine step from active sprite Y positions and adjusts Tiki subject to the movement and collision flags.
Adds the fine step to nonzero actor and projectile Y positions.
Moves the sprite X positions in the opposite direction to $1B0E. On a fine-position borrow it changes screen buffer and copies the colors left.
Subtracts the vertical fine scroll step and shifts whole rows upward when that step borrows.
Adds the fine vertical step and copies the extra color row downward when the fine position wraps.
Changes horizontal and vertical fine scroll fields together. At the vertical boundary it switches matrix and uses the diagonal up-and-right color-copy loop.
Combines the negative horizontal step and positive vertical step, then switches matrix and calls the world's diagonal color-shift operator at $9D0C.
Advances both fine offsets from the same sum and switches display matrix before the $9D8D color-copy path.
Subtracts the shared fine scroll amount in both dimensions and uses the up-and-left RAM color-copy loop at a character boundary.
Toggles the active matrix flag in $07 and XORs $04 into the prepared address bank offset at $053E.
Uses the scrolling mode plus screen-bank flag to choose four address bytes at $9E0A/$9E1A/$9E2A/$9E3A. Patches the two source operands for the matrix shifter.
Once per changed pending-movement count, prepares two destination offsets and copies $B4 or $BE bytes using four patched operands, then advances both source pointers.
Clears the $80 live minimap pattern bytes beginning at $8220.
Clears work state, sets video bank three and the playfield matrix, sets up the status panel, loads round defaults, unpacks its active objects and fills the visible columns.
Selects Tiki's on-screen starting coordinates. World four's boss has separate initial positions for its two sections. World five's third round has its own starting Y.
Iterates object slots 12 down to zero and invokes the map-object routines before the round begins.
Clears the ending-load flag and resets audio or collected-letter state. Preserves the round selector on the late-overlay paths and passes $50 to the busy delay at $20D2.
Installs $4F37 as the first raster IRQ and $20DB as NMI, enables a VIC raster interrupt at $FA, masks CIA 1 interrupts and starts the display.
Saves A, X and Y in zero page, acknowledges the VIC interrupt, advances the sound driver at $6EF9 and returns with the registers restored.
Runs X passes of the Y-decrement loop, with Y starting at zero on each pass. X=0 wraps and runs 256 passes.
Tests the CIA 2 interrupt source and selects a video subphase from $034E. The later phase restores the regular raster vector.
Saves A, acknowledges the raster interrupt and installs $5195 at raster line $55 before returning.
Four initialized values next to the alternate raster entry.
Performs coordinate-window tests in software. It writes the object overlap flags at $035A and the above/below flags at $036A and $036D for the three separately tested slots.
Prepares the source map position and output operands for the newly visible row when the camera steps. Updates the two matrix rows and color RAM through the metatile decoder.
Computes the map byte pointer at $08/$09 from camera X and Y. It extracts the low coordinate bits for the initial glyph offset and remaining cells in the first metatile.
Uses the split metatile pointer directory at $5600/$5700. Places the chosen glyph in both playfield screens and writes that glyph's low color bits to color RAM.
Adjusts the patched matrix and color row destinations before returning to the camera update.
Sets the output column to 39 and enters the shared column renderer.
Converts the camera position to an address within the map at $A000, expands the relevant column from each 4-by-4 metatile and stamps glyph codes into both playfield matrices.
Four lengths used at the visible column's first metatile. The Y offset can start partway through its four glyph rows.
Interleaved addresses for each 40-column display row, used to patch the first playfield screen output operand. The second screen is $400 bytes higher.
Builds all 40 display columns from the initial camera position by invoking the column expander and advancing the map X index.
Low bytes of consecutive 40-column screen row starts. Used at $25F0 to establish collision probe pointers for sprites.
High bytes paired with $258C. The base sequence begins at $C000, and $25F6 combines the high byte with the active screen offset.
Per-sprite indicators that $25D2 sets when the screen Y value can be projected into a playfield probe.
Builds per-object screen and collision probe coordinates from current sprite state. Clears the active probe flag for entries without a Y coordinate.
Uses object Y's prepared screen row and adds the probe offset. Returns the map glyph in Y and that glyph's color and collision attributes in A.
Screen X column values calculated by $25ED and used to index indirectly through the collision row pointer.
Low bytes of per-sprite row pointers derived from the 40-column row table.
High bytes of those row pointers with the current screen offset applied.
Sixteen numeric glyph codes read by $26AC after splitting a byte into its two nibbles.
Scratch copy retained by $26AC to read the original low nibble after printing the high one.
Looks up each nibble of A in the glyph table at $269B and writes them into consecutive status cells starting at $8828 plus Y.
Writes camera and player map fields as two-digit values into several cells of the status buffer via $26AC.
Stores the camera Y coordinate before the object projection routine subtracts the display window height.
Per-slot active state. The object allocator scans for zero and the projection or renderer uses the slot only after its state changes.
Per-object fine Y values. The motion routines update these modulo eight and carry or borrow into world Y.
Thirteen fine X offsets used when projecting objects into sprite positions.
World-space object Y published by the map scan and consumed by the sprite projection.
World-space object X used with the camera position to compute a display coordinate.
Per-slot fields between the world-coordinate arrays and the display colors. The object setup clears this workspace.
Color bytes written by the animation and object routines and transferred to the raster arrays by $28B8.
Sprite pointer bytes for the active object slots. $28BD publishes them for the raster handler.
Projected low X bytes passed to the sprite arrays by $28A7.
Projected sprite Y values, including zero for an off-screen slot.
The ninth X bits for the projected coordinates, transferred to sprite work bytes by $28B3.
Computes screen coordinates from each object's world coordinates and its fine offset. Entries outside the visible bounds get a zero screen coordinate.
Transfers display coordinates, ninth X bits, colors and pointers into the arrays consumed by the raster handler. Expands the special multi-sprite object into adjacent slots.
Derives the ordinary object scan window from camera X, Y and the bound at $0633, with underflow clamping for its left edge.

Scans round records in reverse while slots 6 through 11 are available. A record with eligible flags and coordinates inside the activation window gets bit 7 set and its index copied into the active slot.
Releases a map object's active slot and updates the associated record state when it falls outside the projection window.
Per-phase vertical decrements read by the retiring actor's motion path.
Moves the actor upward by its current step. The color update flips bit one of the value from slot zero, then stores it to the retiring slot. End of sequence clears the relevant records.
Six screen codes copied into the corresponding panel position when the pickup type selects an EXTENDED letter.
Four sprite pointers read in order for a portal's appearance or destruction.
Dispatches a spare object slot's portal state. A visible closed portal starts its sound and score effects. The opening phase advances four sprite frames, then selects the spawned form.
Four masks loaded into $2CB3. The portal spawn-type selector uses the active mask at $2C81.
Reload values for the spawn-cycle countdown at $2CB5.
Two-bit index through the portal spawn masks and intervals at $2CAA/$2CAE.
Current mask applied to the random spawn selector at $2C81.
Number of expiries of the outer countdown before the spawn phase advances.
Current delay before the spawn selection can change.
Applies a two-subpixel horizontal step and a changing signed vertical step after a portal turns into an actor.
Sixteen sprite pointers, indexed by the result of the portal type selector.
Sixteen early colors paired with the display pointers for new arrivals.
Skips actors in temporary action states or with excluded kind values. Direction bits choose a side movement and another flag enables the downward probe.
Probes down and to the facing side. If the actor can descend, clears its ground-step flag and sets the falling flag.
Adds three subpixels to the vertical offset, advances map Y on carry and resumes the grounded state if the probe below hits a blocking tile.
Handles the actor's falling case first. Otherwise probes left and down, turns on obstruction, or advances the fractional X state to the left.
Checks the facing-side probes, reverses direction on the blocking cases and applies the actor's fine X step on the clear path.
Player-relative target in world Y for the steering routine at $340F.
World X target set by the same steering routine and compared against the actor at $3533.
Builds a camera-relative window and checks the map object records for the special bit-6 and bit-0 cases. Uses a separate scan of the first three object slots.
Current sprite pointer written to the special captive display slot. The release sequences adjust it in four-slot steps.
Countdown before the capture or release logic advances its sprite pointer.
Tests the captive-contact latch. A confirmed contact clears the active bit in the map record and joins the release path.
Copies the captive's map coordinates and display color into its reserved object slot, and advances its sprite frame when the hold timer expires.
Steps the captive's shape pointer downward in increments of four. On reaching $EF, clears the release flag and removes the special display slot.
Checks the slot hit flag, then tests $1C to select the follow-up object state. Some cases install an effect sprite and countdown, while an already marked slot is retired immediately.
Tests active direction bits and the actor kind. For kind $17, a timer and collision probe can turn it back, and bit 2 enables the player-relative steering path.
Three per-slot direction values. $3395 uses them to hold Y or step it in either direction.
Three countdowns for the direction change and vertical movement paths.
Runs the timed Y motion for the kind-$16 actor. It sets a new direction and updates the fine Y state, then rejoins the horizontal movement.
Uses the three-state movement byte at $32F5 to choose no step, a downward step or an upward step. Updates world Y after a fine-offset wrap.
Adds the per-actor fractional speed. When it carries, updates vertical motion and subtracts two from the actor's fine X offset.
Adds the speed and advances the fine X offset two subpixels on carry, after applying the vertical step.
Per-slot countdowns for the change of player-relative steering target.
Initializes and refreshes a target relative to the player's camera position and facing. Attempts horizontal and vertical movement subject to the attribute checks from $2610.
Four countdown bytes updated by the oscillating projectile path.
Parallel animation countdowns updated by the trajectory routines.
Signed step scratch used by the oscillation paths and cleared when allocating a new hostile shot.
Uses the owner actor's reserved projectile index. Initializes direction and animation, copies its display coordinates and chooses kind-specific speed, gravity and offset values.
Examines four projectile slots, retiring any active object above or below the bounds. The remaining active slots go to the trajectory dispatch.
Combines the slot index with the probe index base, tests that the probe exists and patches the JMP with the handler indexed by the object's kind.
26 little-endian targets used by $36D8. Several kinds share the same left/right movement code.
Selects cel $C9 and joins the shared directional collision routine.
Checks the prepared probe on the left and subtracts the step from the projectile's X on the clear path.
Checks the corresponding right side and adds a horizontal step when the path permits it.
Uses the projectile phase and current trajectory state before entering the shared movement path.
Clears the projectile's occupied flag and screen position, then clears its owner actor's pending action state.
Sets the step to three and chooses $E0 or $E1 as the shape from the direction bit, then uses the shared left or right movement path.
Signed byte sequence indexed by $04B4. The oscillation handler reverses horizontal direction when it reads a negative step.
Updates the shape sequence according to its direction, then uses the indexed oscillation step to move left or right. Every seventh update selects the next step.
Counts down and advances the directional projectile's shape, wrapping it back into the repeated cel range.
Steps the cel index once the timer expires and wraps $A1 back to $9D.
Moves through the standard left or right collision path with step three and a direction-dependent shape.
Sets a step of two and uses the side-specific projectile cels $CF or $D1.
Uses the direction state to choose either $D0 with a two-pixel Y decrement or $D2 with a two-pixel Y increment. Retires the slot when the probe returns attribute bit 7.
Uses shape $B4 and adjusts Y by the current signed delta. Its delta increases when the four-count timer expires.
Selects shape $EE and adds two to Y before joining the left-probe movement path.
Uses shape $B4, adds two to Y and sets a zero horizontal step before collision handling.
Uses shape $36 and advances six pixels on the horizontal direction path.
Shared timer for the direction-specific projectile path at $39A2.
Uses a countdown byte at $39A1 to switch between the $D9 and $3E shapes and eventually discharge the slot.
Applies the stored Y delta every second pass, with shape $B4 and side-dependent movement.
Reloads an eight-count timer and steps through four cel pointers in the direction selected by the projectile's orientation.
Moves a projectile left by $04C4 and toggles its ninth X bit on borrow.
Moves a projectile right by $04C4 and toggles its ninth X bit on carry.
The paths at $3042–$304F and $35D0–$35D8 initialize these bytes during object setup.
Object-relative row index into the split world-grid pointers at $5800/$5820.
Probe Y plus its requested delta, later reduced to an offset within the metatile.
Probe X relative to its map base, later combined with the within-tile row.

Adds the requested probe deltas to the object's coordinates, reads the map's matching metatile, then tests the chosen glyph's attribute bit 7. Returns carry set for that bit and restores the object indices.
26 little-endian animation pointers for normal movement with set orientation bit. $3E1E selects a pointer by twice the kind byte.
26 little-endian animation pointers for normal movement with clear orientation bit. $3E1E selects a pointer by twice the kind byte.
26 little-endian animation pointers for alternate movement with clear orientation bit. $3E1E selects a pointer by twice the kind byte.
